root_idea.summary: The root centers on entry or penetration into something, especially through a narrow opening; related branches describe poison entering the body, scorching wind penetrating bodies, intimate association, and reconciliation.
root_idea.development: From the idea of an entry or perforation come the senses of a narrow opening, poison, and the penetrating hot wind called سَمُوم. Related extensions describe special intimates as those who enter into private affairs and reconciliation as bringing people into mutual involvement; a separate branch concerns lightness and agility.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested nominal headword with an independently supported lexical sense.
Quran-attested nominal headword with the distinct narrow-opening sense.

senses.definition: A scorching, penetrating hot wind; in Quranic usage, the intense scorching torment associated with such heat.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in expressions for exposure to scorching torment, including نار السموم and في سموم وحميم. The noun denotes the scorching wind or torment, while contextual translations may render the expression as “scorching fire.”

senses.definition: A narrow opening or perforation, especially the eye of a needle.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction in 7:40, the word denotes the tiny opening through which the camel would have to pass. The same lexical branch can describe a narrow hole or passage, but the Quranic example specifically concerns a needle’s eye.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put poison into something, poison it, or give someone poison to drink; a venomous creature may likewise poison or smite a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb; the object may be food or a person receiving poison.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suggest or hint at something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tentatively reported usage whose attribution is not specified in the source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To perforate, pierce, or pass through something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as an apparent usage and connected in the source with the noun مَسَمٌّ, a place of passage or perforation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To probe or examine an affair, seeking to learn its depth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Tropical or extended usage applied to a case or matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make firm or close something, especially to stop or seal an opening.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source notes that this usage may reflect a transcription for سَدَّ, “to close.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rectify or reconcile relations between people, bringing their affairs into agreement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with expressions referring to what lies between people or between two parties.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To string cowries or similar shells.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to وَدَع, shells or cowries used as ornament.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To appropriate a benefit or bounty to a particular object or recipient; to become specific in its object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is reported as both transitive and intransitive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To aim or direct oneself toward someone, or to pursue that person’s way or course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the idiom سَمَمْتُ سَمَّكَ and related expressions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be struck by the wind called سَمُوم; of a day, to be attended by that wind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive usage describing a plant, person, or day affected by the hot wind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Making loops on a girth, or adorning a girth with strung cowries.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun associated with the girth called وَضِين.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To walk or go gently; of a fox, to run in a light or characteristic manner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The fox-related description is a particular application of the general movement sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Poison or venom; also a deadly substance, including particular poisonous substances and plants used as poisons.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Variant vocalizations include سُمّ and سِمّ. The named applications include arsenic and substances used to poison fish or animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the plural, the openings or passages of the human body, including the mouth, nostrils, ears, or clefts of the skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plural usage distinct from the Quranic eye-of-a-needle sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a horse, the thin nasal or tear-channel portions and related veins; the term may also denote a marrow-containing bone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Specialized equine anatomical usage with several reported explanations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A notch in a sword, whether newly made or old.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized application of the opening or cut sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The object of one’s aim or pursuit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the idiom أَصَابَ سَمَّ حَاجَتِهِ, it means to attain the object sought; بَصِيرٌ بِسَمِّ حَاجَتِهِ describes someone skilled in recognizing or attaining it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a fixed idiom, a person’s sole concern or object; by variant interpretations, someone who seeks him, or neither little nor much.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The idiom مَا لَهُ سَمٌّ وَلَا حَمٌّ غَيْرُكَ has several reported explanations, including “he has no concern except you.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: The loop or fastening of the girth called وَضِين.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Plural سُمُوم.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sea-produced shell or cowrie, especially one strung for ornament.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may refer either to the individual shell-like object or to strung cowries collectively.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The vaginal opening or vulvar cleft, including the adjacent parts of the external genital area.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical noun with a specifically feminine reference.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The heart or central growing core of a palm tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also called سَمَّةُ القَلْبِ; distinct from the anatomical sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woven mat or broad tray made from leaves, spread beneath a palm when dates are harvested.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used to catch dates that fall or become scattered during harvesting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The anus.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical noun; the source cross-references the related form سَمَّة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small bird, described as resembling a quail or a swallow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is treated as a collective or plural-like noun in some reports, with سَمَامَة as a singular form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A banner, ensign, or standard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension based on the bird designation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A swift she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A usage of the collective noun used as a singular expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Light, active, agile, slender, or swift.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to people, animals, or other things according to the reported form and context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A distinctive feather or whorl in the middle or side of a horse’s neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A mark regarded favorably by Arab horsemen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person’s physical form, figure, or outward aspect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in descriptions of someone’s pleasing or beautiful appearance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A standing portion or remnant of ruined dwellings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized architectural or archaeological usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seller of sesame.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A professional noun formed from سِمْسِم.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source directs comparison with a related entry under another root for additional detail.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Decorations or embellishments of a ceiling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported without a clearly established singular form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wolf, especially a small-bodied wolf.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The designation is explained by the animal’s lightness or agility.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fox.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate animal designation from the wolf sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A red ant or a biting reddish insect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The singular is also reported as سُمْسُمَة or سِمْسِمَة; the insects are described as biting painfully.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sesame, the well-known plant or its grain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The grain is also associated with the production of sesame oil; a wild variety is separately named in the source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A serpent or a creeping creature resembling one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct lexical use from the name of the sesame plant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A species of bird resembling a swallow, whose eggs are proverbial for being unattainable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: One interpretation of the proverb كَلَّفْتَنِي بَيْضَ السَّمَاسِمِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Red ants.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An alternate interpretation of the same proverb, treating the plural as derived from the red-ant noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Venomous, especially of an animal or creeping thing whose venom is harmful but not normally fatal, such as a scorpion or hornet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine and plural forms are used for venomous animals or groups of them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A species of large gecko or lizard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A zoological name applied to both male and female animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a day, attended by the wind called سَمُوم.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use referring to a day affected by the hot wind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person’s special or intimate circle; distinguished people or close relations.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may denote people of distinction, intimate associates, or particular and choice relations, in contrast with the عامّة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Death.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An explicitly reported but exceptional usage; the source says the usual form for this meaning is سَام, without the gemination and feminine ending.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a nose that is narrow and full in the nostrils.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of the shape of the nose.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of perforation or passage; a pore or opening of the body through which sweat or internal exhalation passes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural مَسَامّ is a technical medical term for bodily pores.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who eats whatever he is able to eat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agent noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a girth, furnished with loops or adorned with strung cowries.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participle describing the girth called وَضِين.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Poisoned or infected with poison; of a person, given poison to drink.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to food or to a person who has received poison.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Smitten by the wind called سَمُوم.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a plant or person affected by the hot wind.
